history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was proposed by Harvard University to explore the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Led by principal investigator Frank Keutsch and his team, the initiative aimed to enhance computer models assessing the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering, specifically solar radiation management. It is crucial to note that SCoPEx was not a deployment test of geoengineering nor intended to cool the planet. The experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola operating at approximately 20 km altitude, designed to release a very small quantity of material—typically calcium carbonate—into a defined volume for analysis. A test conducted in Sweden in 2021 was focused solely on hardware verification and did not involve any emissions. Following recommendations from the SCoPEx Advisory Committee for enhanced societal engagement, Harvard announced in March 2024 that Keutsch would no longer pursue SCoPEx, with plans to reallocate the platform for unrelated stratospheric research. This reflects the importance of prioritizing emissions reductions and maintaining net-zero integrity in climate policy discussions.
